_note: Verified facts for greeting, project and air-quality knowledge answers (backend/agent/knowledge.py). Answers of those kinds may use only numbers from this file or from the live data windows; the number checker enforces it. Sources: CPCB National AQI table and the 'Health Statements for AQI Categories' printed in CPCB's daily AQI bulletin (verbatim, checked 2026-11-13, also in frontend/src/lib/health.ts); CPCB AQI colours and breakpoints (checked 2026-11-06, frontend/src/lib/categories.ts and backend/analysis/aqi.py); India NAAQS 2009 and WHO 2021 24-hour guidelines (frontend/src/lib/categories.ts); the glossary in frontend/src/lib/glossary.ts; data sources and limits from CLAUDE.md and backend/config/known_limits.json. Do not add a fact without its source.

assistant.name: SkyQueryChat
assistant.role: an air-quality analyst for six Indian cities
abilities: PM2.5 and PM10 levels and trends for one city and any period in the data
official CPCB AQI around Diwali 2024, 2025 and 2026
unusually high or low pollution days
how weather (temperature, humidity, wind, rain) is associated with PM levels
data coverage and quality for a city
assistant.how_answers_work: The AI writes the wording; Python calculates every number from the stored data, and a checker confirms each number before the answer is shown, with its source, stations and coverage.
cannot_do: pollutants other than PM2.5 and PM10 (official AQI is shown as published)
medical advice beyond CPCB's health statements

aqi.what: The National Air Quality Index (AQI) published by CPCB turns up to eight pollutants into one number from 0 to 500 and a category. It is an index, not a concentration, so it is never the same as a PM2.5 value.
aqi.bulletin: CPCB publishes a daily AQI bulletin at 4 PM; each city value is the average of the past 24 hours (4 PM to 4 PM).

categories.health_statement: Minor breathing discomfort to sensitive people
Breathing discomfort to the people with lungs, asthma and heart diseases
Breathing discomfort to most people on prolonged exposure
Affects healthy people and seriously impacts those with existing diseases

aqi.health_source: CPCB daily AQI bulletin, 'Health Statements for AQI Categories'

glossary.PM2.5: Particulate Matter 2.5 micrometres or smaller: fine particles that reach deep into the lungs, measured as a concentration in µg/m³.
glossary.PM10: Particulate Matter 10 micrometres or smaller: larger particles such as dust, measured as a concentration in µg/m³. PM10 includes PM2.5.
glossary.AQI: Air Quality Index: an index from 0 to 500 with six categories, not a concentration.
glossary.CPCB: Central Pollution Control Board: India's national pollution regulator. It runs the reference monitors and publishes the daily AQI bulletin.
glossary.µg/m³: micrograms per cubic metre: how much particle mass is in one cubic metre of air.

india_naaqs.source: India National Ambient Air Quality Standards (2009)

sources.name: OpenAQ archive and API
sources.what: measured hourly PM2.5 and PM10 from CPCB reference monitoring stations (primary city averages use reference stations only)

sources.name: CPCB daily AQI bulletins
sources.what: official AQI per city, read from UrbanEmissions' parsed bulletins and CPCB's own bulletin PDFs

sources.name: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API
sources.what: daily temperature, humidity, wind and rain (reanalysis, Copernicus C3S); weather data by Open-Meteo.com, CC BY 4.0

sources.name: OpenCity (CPCB data)
sources.what: Delhi PM around Diwali 2024 and 2025, supporting context only; values above 999 µg/m³ are blank in this source

method: A city value is the equal-weight average of valid station-days at the city's primary reference stations; a station-day needs at least 16 valid hours.
Missing readings are never filled in; days with network-wide gaps are labelled.
Weather results are associations, never causes.
known_limits: Measured data starts on 18 Feb 2025; OpenAQ has no CPCB data from Nov 2022 to that date.
Recent days can be missing until the source publishes them.
Some city-days have network-wide data gaps; they are labelled, and severe ones are left out of weather associations.
Delhi Diwali 2024 and 2025 PM are lower bounds, because the source blanks values above 999 µg/m³; Diwali 2026 Delhi PM comes from OpenAQ and is not compared with them.
Diwali answers use official AQI; measured PM for Diwali 2025 is incomplete outside Delhi.
Weather is modelled reanalysis and may differ from local stations.
